## Pull request overview

Adds a core utility to automatically derive `$expand` fields from object schema metadata and wires it into all major data-fetching plugins so lookup/master_detail fields render expanded objects (labels) instead of raw foreign-key IDs.

**Changes:**
- Introduces `buildExpandFields()` in `@object-ui/core` (with unit tests) and exports it from the core package.
- Injects `$expand` into `dataSource.find()` across plugins (ListView, ObjectGrid, ObjectKanban, ObjectCalendar, ObjectGantt, ObjectMap, ObjectTimeline, ObjectGallery, ObjectView, ObjectAgGrid).
- Updates `ROADMAP.md` to mark `$expand` auto-injection as complete.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 14 out of 14 changed files in this pull request and generated 10 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/core/src/utils/expand-fields.ts | New helper to compute `$expand` fields from schema metadata (+ optional column scoping). |
| packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/expand-fields.test.ts | Unit tests for `buildExpandFields()` behavior and edge cases. |
| packages/core/src/index.ts | Exports the new expand-fields utility from `@object-ui/core`. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx | Computes expand fields from `objectDef` and injects `$expand` into list fetches. |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx | Injects `$expand` into grid query params based on resolved schema + configured columns/fields. |
| packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx | Injects `$expand` into kanban fetches using object schema metadata. |
| packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx | Injects `$expand` into calendar fetches using object schema metadata. |
| packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx | Injects `$expand` into gantt fetches using object schema metadata. |
| packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx | Injects `$expand` into map fetches using object schema metadata. |
| packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx | Adds schema fetch + injects `$expand` into timeline fetches. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/ObjectGallery.tsx | Adds schema fetch + injects `$expand` into gallery fetches. |
| packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx | Injects `$expand` into ObjectView standalone fetch path for non-grid views. |
| packages/plugin-aggrid/src/ObjectAgGridImpl.tsx | Injects `$expand` into AG Grid query params based on object schema. |
| ROADMAP.md | Documents completion of the `$expand` auto-injection work. |
</details>

`objectSchema` is fetched in a separate effect defined after this one, so this effect will typically fire once with `objectSchema === null` (no `$expand`) and then fire again when `objectSchema` is set—duplicating the data request and briefly showing raw lookup IDs. Consider combining schema+data fetch, or early-returning from this effect until `objectSchema` is available for `provider: 'object'`.

`objectSchema` is fetched in a separate effect defined after this one, so the first fetch typically runs with `objectSchema === null` (no `$expand`) and then re-fetches once schema arrives. Consider fetching schema+data together or skipping the initial `find()` until `objectSchema` is loaded for `provider: 'object'` to avoid duplicate requests and ID flicker.

Two issues here: (1) `options: { $top: 100 }` is not honored by the built-in `ApiDataSource`/`ValueDataSource` (they read `params.$top`), so this likely doesn't paginate as intended; (2) because `objectDef` loads asynchronously, the effect will fetch once with no `$expand` and then refetch when `objectDef` arrives. Prefer `{$top: 100}` at the top level and avoid the double-fetch by waiting for objectDef (or fetching schema+data together).

`options: { $top: 100 }` will be ignored by built-in data sources (they read `params.$top`), so this request may return unbounded results. Also, since `objectDef` is fetched separately, the first `find()` runs with `expand === []` and then re-runs when `objectDef` arrives. Consider switching to `{$top: 100}` at the top level and fetching schema+data in a single flow to avoid duplicate requests.

Because `objectDef` is fetched in a separate effect, this data fetch will typically run once with `objectDef === null` (no `$expand`) and then re-run when `objectDef` arrives—duplicating requests and briefly rendering raw lookup IDs. Consider deferring the initial `find()` until objectDef is available (when getObjectSchema is supported) or combining the schema+data load into a single async flow with caching.

`buildExpandFields(resolvedSchema?.fields, ...)` will always return `[]` in the code path where `resolvedSchema` is the "minimal schema stub" (fields `{}`) used when explicit columns/fields are configured. That means `$expand` won't actually be injected for the common explicit-columns scenario. Consider fetching the real object schema (or otherwise providing field metadata) before computing expand fields.

`expandFields` depends on `objectDef?.fields`, but the data-fetch effect runs before `getObjectSchema()` resolves. This causes an initial fetch without `$expand`, followed by a second fetch when `expandFields` updates—extra network load and a brief "raw ID" render. Consider gating the initial fetch until objectDef is available (when getObjectSchema is supported) or combining schema+data fetch into one async flow with caching.

Because `objectSchema` is loaded in a separate effect, this fetch will run once with `objectSchema === null` (so `expand` is empty) and then re-run when `objectSchema` arrives—duplicating the request and momentarily rendering unexpanded lookup IDs. Consider waiting for `objectSchema` (or fetching schema+data in one flow) before calling `find()` when lookup expansion is desired.

`objectSchema` is fetched in a separate effect defined after this one, so the first fetch typically runs with `objectSchema === null` (no `$expand`) and then re-fetches once schema arrives. Consider fetching schema+data together (ObjectGrid already uses this pattern) or skipping the initial `find()` until `objectSchema` is loaded for `provider: 'object'`.
